html:
The Ngarabal are an Aboriginal people of the northern tablelands of New South Wales, around today's Ashford, Tenterfield and Glen Innes. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their high granite country sits on the Great Dividing Range, with rivers flowing west to the Darling basin. Little is recorded in detail about their life before colonisation. Neighbours on the map include the Bundjalung to the east, the Kamilaroi and the Bigambul to the west. Squatters took up the tablelands from the late 1830s, and tin mining followed in the 1870s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
